profile_text.body:
Saltillo's site centers on TouchChat, an iOS app for augmentative and alternative communication (AAC). The company describes it as a dynamic communication solution for people who have difficulty speaking with their natural voice, with easy-to-customize features and a wide range of vocabularies, languages, and voices. The site says TouchChat is built for a variety of communication disorders and offers head tracking, which uses facial recognition on the newest iPad Pro and iPhone models to track head and face movements, plus built-in switch scanning and touch access. It also notes iOS Split View support for viewing two apps side by side, and points users to three different TouchChat apps on the App Store.

The site's harvested text also includes service notices: scheduled maintenance on June 4 from 9:30-10:00 PM ET, and a notice that phone numbers starting with "800" are down, with local numbers starting in "330" given instead (main 330-262-1984, service 330-262-0845).

The held record lists TouchChat under Education & Research AI, with word prediction noted as its AI feature and use as an AAC app for students with communication needs and SLPs. It notes the product was found in research for The AI Ready School and not independently verified, that privacy is not verified, and that pricing comes from a 2022 state AT program list: TouchChat HD $149.99+ on the App Store.
